mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.2%) compresses discount rates applied to equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 7.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions and weak economic growth, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in reduced corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100) during the early stages of a recession signals a contraction in manufacturing output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market discounts worsening corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100 and the economy is in an early recession phase.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) reflects robust consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days by supporting corporate revenue growth and earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the CPI index above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market that fuels wage inflation and potential monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A near-zero federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%) during post-recession recovery periods supports equity valuations through low discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy expands.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.25% and the economy is in a post-recession recovery phase.
